active_reading:
**Mental Note / Sticky Note:**

✅ *Primary Objective of LEGRI: To demonstrate the viability of HgI₂ detectors in space astronomy.*  
🔹 This was the core mission goal of the Low Energy Gamma-Ray Imager (LEGRI), launched in 1997 and operational until 2002.  
🔹 The detector technology (HgI₂) was specifically targeted for use in the **10–100 keV energy range**, enabling both **imaging and spectroscopy** of gamma rays.  
🔹 This focus on HgI₂ detector validation marks a key milestone in space-based gamma-ray instrumentation, proving that such materials can function reliably in space environments for high-energy astrophysical observations.  
🔹 The success of LEGRI in achieving this objective laid foundational groundwork for future missions using similar detector technologies.

📌 *Memorable Anchor:* "LEGRI didn’t just observe gamma rays — it proved HgI₂ could work in space, in the 10–100 keV range."  

This note ensures the significance of the HgI₂ detector is clearly, concisely, and contextually highlighted — directly linking the technical goal to its scientific and engineering impact.
